title: Burying Configurable Data in Low-Level Functions
pattern: Hardcoding default configuration values, fallback parameters, or installation constants inside low-level helper functions instead of exposing them at the bootstrap layer.
why_bad: Hides defaults from maintainers and operators, requiring them to comb through low-level source files to understand the system's baseline behavior. It prevents central overriding and modular configuration swapping.
detection: The assignment of literal constants to configuration fields inside utility or secondary namespaces rather than within a designated configuration/main module.
fix: Hoist all configurable defaults to high-level, centralized metadata structures or pass them down as explicit arguments from the application's entry point.
source: Martin, Robert Cecil - *Clean Code_ A Handbook of Agile Software Craftsmanship* (2008, Prentice Hall).pdf, Chapter 17 (G35).
